title: Golden Tempo surges to Belmont victory, gives Cherie DeVaux another historic win
content:
Kentucky Derby winner Golden Tempo stunned the field for a second time, winning the Belmont Stakes in yet another come-from-behind thriller Saturday at Saratoga Race Course in Saratoga Springs, N.Y.

Trailing 12 lengths off the pace in dead last midway through the race, Golden Tempo and jockey José Ortiz stormed from the outside past eight other horses to overtake Commandment down the stretch for the victory. After passing the half-mile pole, Golden Tempo started to inch off the rail and push to the outskirts of the pack. As pacesetter Powershift began to fall behind down the final stretch, Commandment and Golden Tempo burst ahead, running neck-and-neck before Golden Tempo pulled away and crossed the finish line by more than a length.

“I’m very happy to win today,” a muddied Ortiz, who has a long and successful history of racing at Saratoga Race Course, said on the Fox broadcast following the win. “… But it’s all about (Golden Tempo). We just want him to get better and keep winning these kinds of races, so you know it make him more valuable down the road, and we’re very happy with him. It’s all about him.”

Trainer Cherie DeVaux said before the race that Golden Tempo would “need the perfect trip” to win the Belmont, and the horse delivered yet again.

Despite foregoing a shot at the Triple Crown, Golden Tempo’s Belmont win is historic, as DeVaux became the first female trainer to win two Triple Crown races and the second ever to win the Belmont since Jena Antonucci and horse Archangelo won in 2023. Golden Tempo opted out of the recent Preakness Stakes after trainer DeVaux decided to give her horse ample time to prepare for the Belmont.
